### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Costello syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.502)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5675221)

**Proposed mechanism:** HRAS (HGNC:4834) —DISRUPTS→ RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP43); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP43) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP43) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Activating mutations in HRAS lead to hyperactivation of the RAS/MAPK pathway, contributing to both cardiomyopathy and intellectual disability, the shared phenotypes between the two conditions.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with these diseases who do not harbor gain-of-function mutations in HRAS, or where the RAS/MAPK pathway is not demonstrably hyperactivated. _(variant: rs123456789 (hypothetical HRAS gain-of-function variant))_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the hyperactivated RAS/MAPK pathway could offer therapeutic strategies for both conditions, potentially through MEK inhibitors or other downstream modulators.

#### 2. linear nevus sebaceous syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.451)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5675221)

**Proposed mechanism:** Activating RAS variant (rs75279798) —DISRUPTS→ HRAS (HGNC:4837); Activating RAS variant (rs75279798) —DISRUPTS→ NRAS (HGNC:7928); Activating RAS variant (rs75279798) —DISRUPTS→ KRAS (HGNC:6407); HRAS (HGNC:4837) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-569320); NRAS (HGNC:7928) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-569320); KRAS (HGNC:6407) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-569320); MAPK signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-569320) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin development (HP:0000951); MAPK signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-569320) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal development of skin (HP:0000951). Activating mutations in HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS lead to constitutive activation of the MAPK signaling pathway, which in turn drives abnormal skin development, manifesting as overlapping phenotypes in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of activating mutations in HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS in individuals diagnosed with either MONDO:0014105 or MONDO:0008097, or demonstration that the shared phenotype arises through entirely distinct molecular pathways. _(variant: High frequency (>5%) of the specific disease-associated variant in gnomAD populations would cast doubt on its causal role.)_

**Why it matters:** The shared reliance on RAS signaling pathways suggests that targeted therapies aimed at inhibiting MAPK signaling could be beneficial for both diseases, potentially offering a unified therapeutic strategy.

#### 3. nevus, epidermal  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.426)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5675221)

**Proposed mechanism:** HRAS (HGNC:4830) —INCREASES→ RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP411); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP411) —LEADS_TO→ Cutaneous appendage malformation (HP:0001019); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP411) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermal nevus (HP:0000975). Gain-of-function mutations in HRAS lead to aberrant activation of the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway. This pathway dysregulation, shared between both diseases, drives distinct but related downstream cellular processes, ultimately manifesting as cutaneous appendage malformations in disease A and epidermal nevi in disease B.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the causal variants in disease A and disease B affect completely independent signaling pathways with no downstream convergence, or that the functional consequence of the variants is not a gain-of-function in the RAS/MAPK pathway. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway or its downstream effectors could offer therapeutic strategies for both conditions, potentially through inhibitors of HRAS, MEK, or ERK.

Dysregulation of the MAPK cascade affects cell proliferation and differentiation, contributing to the phenotypes of Noonan syndrome and large congenital melanocytic nevus.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of gain-of-function mutations in HRAS or other RAS pathway components in individuals with either disease, or demonstration that the RAS signaling pathway is not significantly altered in affected tissues. _(variant: rs121434463)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the RAS signaling pathway or its downstream effectors could offer therapeutic strategies for both Noonan syndrome and congenital melanocytic nevi, potentially through MEK inhibitors or other pathway modulators.

#### 5. thyroid cancer, nonmedullary, 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.400)

**Proposed mechanism:** HRAS (HGNC:4830) —DISRUPTS→ RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP406); NRAS (HGNC:7909) —DISRUPTS→ RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP406); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP406) —LEADS_TO→ Thyroid follicular cell hyperplasia (HP:0030040); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP406) —LEADS_TO→ Thyroid cancer (MONDO:0008566); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP406) —LEADS_TO→ Thyroid dysgenesis (HP:0011674); RAS/MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP406) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital hypothyroidism (HP:0000870). This aberrant signaling contributes to thyroid follicular cell hyperplasia and subsequent development of nonmedullary thyroid cancer (Disease B). In parallel, dysregulation of this pathway via HRAS/NRAS mutations can also lead to thyroid dysgenesis and congenital hypothyroidism (Disease A).

**How to falsify it:** Absence of activating mutations in HRAS or NRAS in patients with both thyroid dysgenesis/congenital hypothyroidism and nonmedullary thyroid cancer, or identification of distinct, non-RAS/MAPK related causal pathways for each disease. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a high allele frequency (>0.1%) for specific gain-of-function variants in HRAS or NRAS in the general population would also challenge their exclusive role in these rare diseases.)_

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-202670, Reactome:R-HSA-5675221)

Loss-of-function mutations in PPP2CA disrupt the assembly and activity of the Protein Phosphatase 2 (PP2A) complex. This dysregulation of PP2A activity impacts multiple downstream cellular processes, ultimately leading to the phenotypes of microcephaly, intellectual disability, and seizures observed in both Houge-Janssens syndrome 3 and a subset of other neurodevelopmental disorders.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in PPP2CA exhibiting a completely distinct set of phenotypes without any overlap in intellectual disability or seizures, or demonstration that the identified variants do not impact PP2A complex assembly or activity. _(variant: The presence of common variants in the gnomAD database with allele frequencies > 1% in the coding region of PPP2CA that are associated with normal neurodevelopment.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PPP2CA in these distinct but phenotypically overlapping conditions could facilitate the development of targeted therapies aimed at modulating PP2A activity or its downstream effectors, potentially benefiting patients with both Houge-Janssens syndrome 3 and other neurodevelopmental disorders with similar genetic underpinnings.
